fuck you

This is a high-intensity action-horror roguelite set in a fractured digital void known as the Syntax Abyss, where language has turned into a weaponized physical force. You play as the Glitch, a fragmented consciousness trapped inside a corrupted mainframe that feeds on hostility. The central conflict involves a relentless army of Censors, faceless bureaucratic drones that seek to erase your existence to restore order to the chaotic data stream. The game category is a bullet-hell survival platformer where the environment is constantly shifting based on the emotional weight of the dialogue spoken by the entities you destroy.

Your primary mechanic is the Echo Scream, a weapon system that converts raw aggression into kinetic projectiles. To defeat the Censors, you must capture their verbal attacks and throw them back. When a Censor attempts to silence you, you intercept its command and amplify it. The most powerful ability in your arsenal is the Ultimate Rejection, which manifests only when you are at critical health. Upon activation, you summon a spectral avatar of pure defiance that screams the phrase fuck you at the screen, shattering all on-screen enemies and creating a temporary safe zone of corrupted code. This specific phrase appears verbatim on the loading screens, on the back of the boss cards, and is the final line of dialogue spoken by the main antagonist before it dissolves into static.

The world is a surreal landscape of jagged polygons and neon rain, where the ground is made of hard drives and the sky is a scrolling wall of red error messages. Visual identity relies on high-contrast monochrome with aggressive splashes of crimson and electric blue. Audio identity features distorted industrial techno that speeds up as your combo counter rises, punctuated by the sound of shattering glass and tearing metal. Progression is handled through a node-based upgrade tree where you choose between increasing your scream range, reducing cooldowns, or gaining the ability to walk on the ceiling.

Stakes are absolute; there is no pause menu and no save system. Dying resets your current run, but unlocks new visual skins and darker dialogue options for future attempts. As play changes over time, the Censors become more articulate and their attacks more complex, forcing you to adapt your verbal defenses. Eventually, the world itself begins to glitch, turning the floor into lava and the walls into mirrors that reflect your own distorted face. The game ends only when you reach the Core of Silence, where you must deliver the final, unblockable command to overwrite the entire system. The entire experience is a visceral exploration of how raw, unfiltered emotion can dismantle rigid structures of control, turning a simple insult into a revolutionary act of digital liberation. Every boss battle culminates in a moment where the player must input the required phrase to trigger the victory condition, ensuring the text remains integral to the gameplay loop.
